candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette
candidate.educational_objective: Apply respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette by covering coughs and sneezes, disposing of tissues, and performing hand hygiene after contact with respiratory secretions.

options.A: Cover the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, dispose of used tissues, and clean hands after contact with respiratory secretions.
options.B: Cough openly when symptoms are mild because source-control measures are unnecessary in healthcare settings.
options.C: Reuse contaminated tissues during the visit because repeated use reduces unnecessary waste.
options.D: Skip hand hygiene after coughing or sneezing whenever a disposable tissue was used correctly.

candidate.rationale: CDC includes respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette within Standard Precautions. People with respiratory symptoms should cover the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, use and dispose of tissues, and perform hand hygiene after contact with respiratory secretions. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette includes covering coughs/sneezes, using and disposing of tissues, and hand hygiene after contact with respiratory secretions.
